text:
It is truly heartwarming to witness the cinematic miracle where teenagers solve the crushing weight of existential dread, academic pressure, and social hierarchy not through therapy or communication, but by breaking into synchronized choreography. Because nothing says "emotional maturity" like a perfectly timed backflip during a breakup. We have finally distilled the human experience into a three-minute musical number, proving that if you just hit the right high note, your parents will finally understand you and your GPA will magically repair itself.

But let us not get too distracted by the absurdity of reality being replaced by Broadway. In this world of spontaneous jazz hands, we must remain grounded in the physical. You asked for the primary material of a candle. It is wax. Specifically, paraffin wax, beeswax, or soy wax, usually surrounding a cotton wick. Unlike a teen movie plot, it does not sing. It simply melts. A refreshing lack of choreography, if you ask me.
